nodes.title: Seasonal naive baseline

nodes.title: Rolling SARIMA

nodes.title: Prophet
nodes.summary: Trend, daily/weekly/annual seasonal components with limited tuning; static holdout forecasts.

nodes.title: XGBoost
nodes.summary: Tree boosting on calendar and historical-demand features.

nodes.title: Weather-enhanced XGBoost
nodes.summary: XGBoost using additional observed/lagged temperature and heating/cooling predictors.

nodes.title: Weather-enhanced rolling SARIMAX
nodes.summary: Rolling SARIMA-family model with exogenous weather predictors.

nodes.title: Official 50/50 hybrid
nodes.summary: Arithmetic mean of rolling SARIMA and weather-enhanced XGBoost hourly forecasts; not a separately retrained model.

nodes.title: ERCOT published day-ahead benchmark
nodes.summary: External forecast generated by ERCOT, not a model trained by the team.

nodes.title: Revise static full-year SARIMA to rolling 24h
nodes.summary: Initial long-range fixed forecast drifted implausibly, prompting rolling windows and updates.

nodes.title: Distinguish magnitude from directional error
nodes.summary: MAE is nonnegative; signed forecast minus actual error indicates over- versus underprediction.

nodes.title: Do SARIMA and Weather XGBoost make different errors?
nodes.summary: Use paired signed-error plots to investigate whether averaging could cancel some errors; correlation alone does not guarantee gain.

nodes.title: Chronological exploratory hybrid-weight check
nodes.summary: Choose blend weight on Oct. 2025–Mar. 2026 hours, then assess on Apr.–Sep. 2026; does not replace official 50/50 model.

nodes.title: Demand varies strongly by hour and season
nodes.summary: Summer afternoon peaks and variable daily patterns motivate calendar and lag predictors; descriptive association alone does not prove model skill.

nodes.title: Weather improved XGBoost, not tested SARIMAX
nodes.summary: Weather XGBoost outperformed original XGBoost overall; weather SARIMAX did not outperform rolling SARIMA.

nodes.title: Hybrid leads team overall
nodes.summary: On 8,640 matched hours, ERCOT MAE ≈1,135; hybrid ≈2,006; weather XGB ≈2,477; naive ≈4,205 MWh. Hybrid improves ≈52% versus naive.

nodes.title: ERCOT remains more accurate overall
nodes.summary: External operator benchmark beats all team models on 8,640 matched hours; this is not a fair same-issuance contest.

nodes.title: One high-demand week illustrates forecast shape
nodes.summary: Jul. 19–25, 2026 shows recurring load rises and falls and differing peak magnitudes; case study does not establish model rankings.

nodes.title: Peak-hour model ranking reverses
nodes.summary: Top 1% observed demand: 88 matched hours, cutoff ~87,966 MWh; rolling SARIMA MAE ~1,242, weather SARIMAX ~1,176, hybrid ~3,189, weather XGBoost ~6,421 MWh.

nodes.title: Both XGBoost variants underforecasted all top-1% hours
nodes.summary: On retrospective top 1% (88 matched hours), XGBoost and weather XGBoost underpredicted every hour.

nodes.title: Tree extrapolation is a possible explanation
nodes.summary: Tree-based boosted methods may be limited at unseen record load magnitudes while rolling SARIMA adapts to recent observations; plausible interpretation, not causal proof.

nodes.title: ERCOT error rose only modestly in top decile
nodes.summary: Historical ERCOT MAE about 1,132 MWh outside top demand decile versus 1,163 within; challenged assumption that high load automatically means much larger errors.

nodes.title: 50/50 beat tuned earlier-weight blend on later split
nodes.summary: Exploratory earlier-selected SARIMA weight ~36% did not beat fixed 50/50 blend on later assessment; not a prospectively optimized operational rule.

nodes.title: Models have different error regimes
nodes.summary: Notebook F26–F33 compare hour/month/season-specific MAE with each model’s own overall MAE; own-average improvement is not the same as beating baseline or ERCOT.
